evidence.reason: The parser is explicitly reading NUL-delimited `git ls-files --stage -z` output, so tracked filenames may legally contain line breaks. In JavaScript, `.` does not match `\n`, `\r`, or Unicode line separators, so a tracked path containing an internal newline fails the `(.+)` capture and throws `terminal foreign index entry unsupported`, aborting settlement even when the offending path is unchanged. This is an implementation defect in existing intended verification behavior; the smallest fix is to capture the filename without relying on dot semantics, e.g. match the remainder up to the already-established NUL boundary.
